script.t: Good morning, Seaview Hotel. How can I help you?
Hello. I'd like to book a room for next weekend, please. From Friday to Sunday.
So two nights. Is that a single or a double room?
A double room, please. It's for me and my wife. It's our wedding anniversary.
Congratulations! We have a double room with a sea view for ninety-five pounds a night, or one without a view for seventy-five.
The one with the sea view, please. It's a special weekend. Is breakfast included?
Yes, breakfast is included, from seven to ten. And the restaurant is open for dinner every evening.
Great. Is there parking at the hotel?
Yes, there's a car park behind the hotel. It's free for guests. Can I have your name, please?
Yes, it's Peter Davies. D-A-V-I-E-S.
Thank you, Mr Davies. And what time will you arrive on Friday?
Probably around six in the evening. We're driving from Birmingham.
That's fine. I'll put some flowers in the room for your anniversary.

script.t: Hi Sam, it's Karen from the office. I'm sorry to call you on your day off, but there's been a change of plan for tomorrow. The meeting with the people from Green Energy was at ten o'clock, but now it's at nine, because they have to catch a plane at twelve. So please come in a bit earlier, at about half past eight. We need to prepare the meeting room before they arrive. Also, can you bring your laptop? Mine isn't working and I need to show them the new photos. Oh, and they told me that one of them doesn't eat meat, so please don't order the chicken sandwiches. Get the cheese ones instead. After the meeting, you can leave early, at three, because you are working on Saturday. Call me back if there's a problem. Thanks, Sam. Bye!

script.t: Today we're talking to Nina Walker, who is fifteen and the best young swimmer in our town. Nina, when did you start swimming?
When I was four. My dad took me to the pool every Sunday, and I loved it from the first day.
How often do you train now?
Six days a week. I swim before school, from six to half past seven, and then again after school for an hour.
That's a lot! Is it difficult to do your homework?
Sometimes. I do my homework on the bus and in the evenings. My teachers help me a lot.
What was your best moment so far?
Last summer I won a silver medal in the national championships. I was so happy, I cried!
And what do you do on your free day?
I sleep! And I go shopping with my friends or watch films.
What's your dream?
To swim in the Olympic Games one day.

title: Easy pancakes
model: Cambridge A2 Key – Listening Part 4 (short talk)

script.t: Hello and welcome to Easy Cooking. Today we're making pancakes. They're perfect for breakfast at the weekend, and children love them. You only need four things: one cup of flour, one egg, one cup of milk and a little butter. First, put the flour in a big bowl. Then add the egg and the milk, and mix everything together until it's smooth. Don't worry if there are a few small lumps. Next, put a little butter in a frying pan and wait until it's hot. Pour in some of the mixture and cook it for about one minute. When you see small bubbles on top, turn the pancake over and cook the other side for thirty seconds. That's it! You can eat your pancakes with honey, fruit or chocolate. My favourite is lemon and sugar. This recipe makes about eight pancakes, enough for a family of four. Enjoy!

script.t: Hello, can I help you?
Yes, I bought this jacket here last week, and I'd like to change it.
Of course. What's the problem with it?
It's too small. I bought a medium, but I need a large. Also, I think I prefer it in a different colour. This one is grey.
Let me check. We have it in large in black, blue and dark green.
Oh, I like the green one. Can I try it on?
Sure, the changing rooms are over there, next to the stairs.
Thanks... Yes, this one is perfect. It's much better.
Great. Do you have your receipt?
Yes, here it is.
Thank you. The green one is the same price, sixty pounds, so you don't need to pay anything. Would you like a bag?
No thanks, I'll wear it now. It's cold outside!

script.t: Do you want to learn something new this autumn? The City College has lots of evening classes for adults. Classes start on the twenty-third of September and finish in December. There's a photography course on Mondays, where you can learn how to take great photos with your phone. On Tuesdays, there's a Spanish class for beginners. The teacher, Maria, is from Seville. On Wednesdays, you can try our pottery class and make your own cups and plates. And on Thursdays, there's a popular cooking class. This year the theme is Indian food. All classes are from seven to nine pm and cost one hundred and twenty pounds for the whole course. If you are over sixty or a student, it's only eighty pounds. You can book online or visit the college office, which is open from nine to five, Monday to Friday.

script.t: Olivia, it's Ben's birthday on Saturday. What can we buy him?
Hmm. He likes music. What about a CD?
Nobody listens to CDs anymore! He listens to everything on his phone.
You're right. What about a book? He reads a lot.
Yes, but he has hundreds of books. I don't know which ones he has.
OK... He loves cooking, doesn't he? We could buy him a cooking class.
That's a great idea! There's a Japanese cooking class in town. He loves sushi.
How much is it?
Fifty pounds, I think. So twenty-five each.
That's a bit expensive for me this month. Can we ask Lily to share it too?
Good idea. Then it's about seventeen pounds each. I'll call her tonight.
And I'll make him a birthday card.

script.t: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Hilltop Castle. My name is James and I'm your guide today. The castle is more than eight hundred years old. A rich family lived here for five hundred years, but now it's a museum. Our tour takes about one hour. First, we'll visit the great hall, where the family had big parties with music and dancing. Then we'll go up to the tower. There are one hundred and fifty steps, so it's not easy, but the view from the top is wonderful. On a clear day, you can see the sea. After that, we'll visit the old kitchen. Please don't touch anything in the rooms, and remember that you can take photos, but not with a flash. At the end of the tour, there's a café and a gift shop near the main gate. Are there any questions? No? OK, follow me, please.

script.t: Hi there. What can I do for you?
Hi. There's a problem with my phone. The battery doesn't last. I charge it at night, but by lunchtime it's empty.
How old is the phone?
About three years old.
Then I think it needs a new battery. That's normal after two or three years.
Can you change it here?
Yes, we can. It costs forty-five euros, and it takes about two hours.
Two hours? Can't you do it faster? I need my phone for work.
Sorry, we're very busy today. But you can leave it now and come back at four o'clock.
OK, that's fine. I'll go and have lunch. Do I need to pay now?
No, you can pay when you collect it. Can you write your name and phone number here, please? Your work number is fine.
Sure. And please be careful with the photos. There are lots of pictures of my kids.
Don't worry. Changing the battery doesn't delete anything.

title: Our school garden
model: Cambridge A2 Key – Listening Part 4 (short talk)

script.t: Hi everyone. I'm Hannah, and I'm in class 9B. I want to tell you about our school garden. Two years ago, there was only grass behind the sports hall. Now we have a big vegetable garden! We grow potatoes, carrots, tomatoes and lots of herbs. The school kitchen uses our vegetables for lunch, so we eat food that we grew ourselves. We also have three beehives, and last year we got twenty jars of honey. We sold them at the school fair and used the money to buy new tools. About thirty students work in the garden. We meet every Friday after school, from three thirty to five. You don't need to know anything about plants. Mr Patel, our biology teacher, teaches us everything. It's a great way to make friends and be outside. If you want to join, write your name on the list outside the library.
